questions.q: What is the correct order of Tableau's six-stage filter sequence?
options: Extract Filters, Data Source Filters, Context Filters, Dimension Filters, Measure Filters, Table Calc Filters
Table Calc Filters, Measure Filters, Dimension Filters, Context Filters, Data Source Filters, Extract Filters
Dimension Filters, Measure Filters, Context Filters, Extract Filters, Data Source Filters, Table Calc Filters
All six stages run simultaneously with no fixed order
questions.explain: Tableau always processes filters in this fixed sequence: Extract, Data Source, Context, Dimension, Measure, then Table Calc filters.

questions.q: Why do Table Calc Filters have to run last?
options: A table calculation needs the rest of the view's data already assembled in order to compute in the first place
Tableau processes filters in a random order and Table Calc Filters happen to finish last most of the time
Table Calc Filters are optional and never actually run
Table Calc Filters run first, not last
questions.explain: A table calculation is computed against the view's already-assembled data, so any filter based on one can only be applied after everything else.

questions.q: Why can a Dimension Filter never bring back a row that a Context Filter already excluded?
options: Each stage in the order of operations only ever sees rows that survived every earlier stage
Dimension Filters and Context Filters run at the exact same time
Context Filters can be overridden by any later filter
Dimension Filters always run before Context Filters
questions.explain: Because Context Filters (stage 3) run before Dimension Filters (stage 4), any row a Context Filter excludes is simply gone by the time a Dimension Filter runs.

questions.q: In the City/Customer Name sort example from this lesson, why does the sort only order customers within New York City rather than the whole dataset?
options: The City filter (a dimension filter) runs before the sort, so the sort only ever orders the rows that already survived filtering
Tableau cannot sort filtered data under any circumstances
The sort is applied before the filter, which is why it looks incomplete
Sorting and filtering are unrelated features with no interaction
questions.explain: Filtering happens before sorting in the order of operations, so the sort operates only on whatever rows the City filter has already narrowed the view down to.

questions.q: When a filter seems to 'not be working,' what does this lesson recommend checking first?
options: Whether an earlier stage — like a context filter or extract filter — already excluded the rows you expected the current filter to include
Whether the workbook needs to be completely rebuilt from scratch
Whether the filter's field name is spelled correctly, which is always the cause
Whether Tableau needs to be reinstalled
questions.explain: Since later stages can never recover rows an earlier stage excluded, debugging an unexpected filter result usually means checking what ran before it in the order of operations.
